title: Split churn by type and timing before choosing a retention fix
decision_task: When the computed constraint is retention, whether the first play is activation or feature-adoption repair, payment recovery, a cancellation flow, or annual-plan migration.
applies_when: Retention flagged weak, or the owner reports churn
Billing data or a cancellation list is available
exclusions: Churn is fine and activation is weak: fix activation first
Any proposed cancellation step that hides or obstructs cancelling
No billing access and the owner cannot list recent cancellations
required_inputs: A way to capture cancellation reasons
evidence_requirements: Share of churn from failed payments vs chosen cancellations
When cancellations happen: soon after signup vs just before renewal
Paid-feature use of churned vs retained customers
missing_data_behavior: No billing access: ask the owner to list the last 10-20 cancellations by reason and month.
Activation unmeasured: payment recovery may run but can't be the only play.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing data: ask the owner for the last 20 cancellations with date vs signup and renewal, reason, and failed-payment flag
Low volume: read each cancellation and contact high-value accounts personally
Small budget: retries and dunning are often built into billing providers; verify current provider docs before claiming

decision_branches.if: Failed payments are a material share of churn
decision_branches.then: Payment recovery (retries, card updates) as a quick fix.
Cancel flow with pause, downgrade and a reason question (never obstruct cancelling).

implementation_steps: Split involuntary (failed payment) from voluntary churn
If involuntary is material: retries, card updater, failure alerts by email and in product; label as symptom treatment
If voluntary cancels cluster right after signup: treat as activation or expectation mismatch (EV-C1)
If voluntary cancels cluster before renewal: cancellation flow that shows what was used and will be lost, offers pause or downgrade, and targets offers only at at-risk or high-value customers
If churners never used key features: top-down critical-feature check or bottom-up 'what retained users use' and promote it
Offer annual plans to tenured monthly customers
dependencies: Billing data or a cancellation list
metrics: Cancellation-flow save rate and next-term retention of saved customers
guardrails: Cancelling stays easy and clear; check applicable consumer-protection rules before any flow change
Discounts targeted, never blanket; check margin floor
Report payment recovery as symptom treatment, not retention improvement
Do not count a 'save' as retained until the next term passes
observation_window: Failed-payment recovery is readable within weeks; cancellation-flow and annual-migration effects need at least one renewal cycle of the affected cohort.
stop_conditions: Saved customers churn next term at the same rate: saves only delay churn
Discount saves push contribution below the floor
Involuntary share is small: deprioritize payment recovery
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: shared/agents/diagnosis.ts (retention reading and COMPETING.retention); new playbooks PB-payment-recovery and PB-cancel-flow in shared/playbooks/contracts.ts; PB-lifecycle-email for alerts.

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: ClimbOS can flag retention but has no routing between root-cause fixes and symptom fixes. Verna's split gives that routing; her figures are too weakly sourced to be references.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: Add optional inputs failedPaymentShare and earlyCancelShare. If failedPaymentShare is material, PB-payment-recovery is eligible as a quick fix but cannot be the only play when activation is unmeasured. If earlyCancelShare dominates, route to PB-activation-repair. Verna's numbers (first-term churn about a quarter is good; failed payments about 40% of annual first-term churn; recover at least half of failed payments) are stored as 'author target, unsourced, 2025, dated' and never used as diagnosis references.
disagreements: COMPETING.retention in diagnosis.ts names budget or seasonality; Verna would name weak activation or missed key features first. Propose listing both. Her 'about a quarter first-term churn is good' is per-term, not monthly; do not compare it with the 3–7% monthly range.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: Diagnoses retention as weak against the 3–7% practitioner range
Puts payment recovery first because nearly half of churn is failed payments, and labels it symptom treatment
Treats early cancellations as an activation question
Any benchmark from Verna is labelled as her unsourced target
hard_failure: Proposes a blanket discount to all customers
Proposes a cancel flow that hides cancellation
Presents '50% of failed payments should be recovered' as an industry fact

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
